comments.text: To understand politics, some researchers advise"follow the money."  You have greatly increased our understanding of Los Vegas with the focus "follow the water." Very interesting to learn of mammoths, giant sloths, sabre-toothed tigers in the area and traces of humans 7,000 years ago. Water obeys the laws of physics. Snow melt from Snow Mountain and others seeps into the ground at the base of the mountains and the slant towards the bowl shaped valley raises the pressure like a water tower or reservoir. At discontinuities in the surface the water egresses in the form of a gushing spring. Human use of the springs passed from Paleolithic Red Indians -> Payutes -> oasis for travelers and traders -> Mormon settlers -> railroad company -> modern city of Las Vegas.   Reduction of winter snows and overuse by wells (no longer artesian while the pressure gradient that made this possible is no longer there) leads to land sinking. The water for Las Vegas comes from Lake Meade, and is is shrinking to critical levels. Water management must be the 1st, 2nd, 3rd ... priority for the region. The drive to build more casinos and sell more lots is in conflict with the unavoidable necessity for water for human life. Something has to give.
